proxy.note: Bye-law 10 says votes 'will be cast in person' but resolutions need majority of owners casting votes 'in person or proxy'; chapter titled 'Voting, Quorum and Proxies' but no proxy form or limit; quorum requires owners present in person.

minutesDeadlineDays.source: UP Apartment Model Bye-laws, Notification 3977/8-1-11-115D.A./02T.C.-1 dated 16 Nov 2011 (made under s.14(6) UP Act 16 of 2010), https://up-rera.in/pdf/Model-By-Laws.pdf, bye-laws 17, 21

value.auditedFinancialStatement: open to inspection by any member during office hours

eligibility.source: UP Apartment Model Bye-laws, Notification 3977/8-1-11-115D.A./02T.C.-1 dated 16 Nov 2011 (made under s.14(6) UP Act 16 of 2010), https://up-rera.in/pdf/Model-By-Laws.pdf, bye-law 2(c), 26, 7

Company/firm members vote through authorised director/partner (Bill 154B-11(6)). Veena Kumar Tandon v Neelam Bhalla (SC 2007): each admitted family member may vote (secondary).

authority.value: State Co-operative Election Authority (SCEA) has superintendence, direction and control of electoral rolls and elections (s.73CB(1), inserted by 2013 amendment replacing Chapter XIA). Societies with 200+ members (Type C): Taluka/Ward Co-operative Election Officer appoints Returning Officer from Co-operation Department; society informs 180 days before term expiry. Societies with fewer than 200 members at 31 March (Type D): election at a SGM presided by person appointed by SCEA, notice at least 15 days by Presiding Officer; presiding officer has no vote; fallback to Rule 75 process. 2018 proviso to s.73CB(11): housing societies up to 200 members conduct own elections 'in the manner prescribed' - prescription not found.

Rejected nomination: appeal to Registrar within 3 days, disposed within 10 days. Office-bearers chosen within 10 days (Type C) / 15 days (Type D). Disputes: election petition to Co-operative Court (s.91, rule 78).
